actual_author_read_scope: Complete scientific main text through p385 L751; Methods, Results, Tables 1–2 and figure captions read. No raw PDF or figure rasters.

claims.paraphrase: DmpF-expressing E. coli extracts formed acetyl-CoA from acetaldehyde/CoA/NAD; unrelated dmpQ control and native acetate-growth controls were distinct. Propionaldehyde was an alternate substrate.

Phenol-grown CF600 DmpFG copurified; N termini identified DmpF and DmpG. Measured bands were 34.5/40 kDa, with inferred sequence masses 32.5/37.5 kDa. Apparent 148 kDa solution mass supported two of each subunit.

Manganese stimulated aldolase; zinc inhibited; magnesium/calcium did not stimulate. NADH stimulated aldolase in delayed-addition controls. Direct NADH binding to DmpG or an allosteric transmission mechanism was not demonstrated.
EDTA dialysis left basal aldolase activity; added manganese activation did not settle whether tightly bound metal was essential.
Hydrolyzed S-lactone substrate gave incomplete pyruvate recovery. Aldehyde and NAD/NADP comparisons were assay-specific; alternate substrates must not become formal catechol-route products.

Channeling, protection from toxicity and ATP benefit were proposals. Alternative acetaldehyde-metabolizing activities existed; failed detection of DmpG alone could reflect expression or assay sensitivity.
A single Results sentence associates propionaldehyde with 3-methylcatechol, conflicting with abstract/discussion mapping to 4-methyl/3,4-dimethylcatechol. Preserve the internal inconsistency.

limits: This establishes the shared terminal acylating machinery in CF600, not all seven reactions in every listed organism.
